comparisons.peer_summary: AMD focuses its R&D on designing next-generation CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, Adaptive SoCs, accelerators, SOMs, and SmartNICs, along with associated software and hardware design tools.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD disclose their core R&D focus areas for next-generation products. Qualcomm explicitly states it makes investments to provide integrated circuit chipsets for specific end-markets including mobile, automotive, and IoT. Similarly, AMD details its R&D focus on delivering next-generation processors (CPU/GPU), FPGAs, and adaptive SoCs, while also highlighting a focus on security-integrated ICs and associated software. While AMD lists a broader range of product types including accelerators and SmartNICs not explicitly mentioned in the Qualcomm snippet, both companies anchor their R&D strategies in the design of advanced computing platforms for similar high-growth segments.

sentences.text: We make investments to provide our integrated circuit customers with chipsets designed on leading-edge technology nodes that combine multiple technologies for use in mobile devices; automotive systems for connectivity, digital cockpit and ADAS/AD; and IoT including consumer electronic devices, industrial devices and edge networking products.
We support Android, Windows, Linux and other client software environments in our chipsets.

Our main area of focus is on delivering the next generation of processors (CPU and GPU), FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs, accelerators (adaptive, graphics and DPU), SOMs and SmartNICs and associated software.

We focus on designing, with security in mind, new integrated circuits (ICs) with improved performance and performance-per-watt in advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes, the design of logic and interface IP, advanced packaging technologies, and heterogeneous integration technologies.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D investment strategy and competitive advantage
comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom commits to continuous investment in product development and enhancement, leveraging proprietary R&D to gain competitive advantages through performance differentiation. The company also opportunistically seeks to enhance capabilities through the acquisition of engineers and technologies, while maintaining significant R&D spending to preserve its competitive position.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Broadcom explicitly describe using acquisitions and investments to enhance their R&D capabilities and product pipelines. Qualcomm states it engages in acquisitions to 'meet certain technology needs' and 'support the design and introduction of new products.' Broadcom mirrors this strategy, noting it 'opportunistically seeks to enhance our capabilities through the acquisition of engineers with complementary research and development skills and complementary technologies.' Both firms treat acquisition as a complement to their internal continuous investment in product development.

comparisons.peer_summary: MCPs integrate multiple memory types, generally LPDDR, into single packages for embedded IoT, automotive, mobile, and industrial devices where space and power efficiency are critical.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Micron disclose the specific applications for their advanced hardware designs, with significant overlap in automotive and IoT segments. Qualcomm highlights that its chipsets are designed for use in 'automotive systems for connectivity, digital cockpit and ADAS/AD' and 'IoT including consumer electronic devices, industrial devices and edge networking products.' Micron similarly describes its Multi-Chip Packages (MCPs) as being used in 'embedded internet of things (IoT) applications, automotive systems, mobile devices, and industrial devices.' While Qualcomm focuses on integrated circuit chipsets for connectivity/computing and Micron focuses on memory integration, they both explicitly target the same high-growth automotive and IoT ecosystems for their respective product innovations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Focus on Accelerated Computing Markets and Platform Components
comparisons.peer_summary: The company specializes in markets where its computing platforms provide acceleration for applications, incorporating processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services. These platforms address four large markets: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA disclose their focus on providing complete, integrated platforms rather than just components, targeting specific large markets. Qualcomm describes making investments to provide 'integrated circuit customers with chipsets... that combine multiple technologies' for use in 'mobile devices; automotive systems... and IoT.' NVIDIA states its computing platforms 'incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services' to address large markets including 'Automotive.' Both companies emphasize a holistic platform approach (combining hardware, software, and system-level integration) to serve the automotive and mobile/IoT sectors.
